T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
T1003.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, often through LSASS memory dumping or registry hives.

T1059.001.name: PowerShell Scripting
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, often with bypass flags (-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -EncodedCommand).

T1218.name: System Binary Proxy Execution (LOLbins)
T1218.description: Adversaries may use trusted native binaries such as certutil, mshta, rundll32, or regsvr32 to download payloads or bypass application whitelisting.

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact (Ransomware)
T1486.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability, often deleting volume shadow copies via vssadmin or wmic beforehand.

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol (C2)
T1071.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, WebSockets, DNS) to blend in with legitimate network traffic.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts (Brute Force / Credential Abuse)
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts through brute force (event 4625 bursts) or password spraying.

T1070.name: Indicator Removal (Event Log Clearing)
T1070.description: Adversaries may delete system and security event logs (Event ID 1102 / 104) to destroy evidence of their activities.
